prompt:
Write 10 short claim log entries (one to three sentences each) by an auto insurance adjuster for a hit while turning left claim, in time order. Injury: shoulder injury. The claimant is not represented by a lawyer. Start each entry on a new line with 'Entry 1:', 'Entry 2:' and so on. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1004; do not mention it.) Work these facts into the text naturally, in your own words, without listing them:
- The reported injury matches the kind and force of the crash well.
- Treatment followed a usual course and tapered off as the patient improved.
- Years ago the patient had a small strain in the same area that healed fully.
- Witnesses, photos and the other driver all confirm the accident happened as described.
- The vehicle damage matches the described impact.
- The claimant told the same account in every conversation.
- The police and witnesses confirm the claimant was in the vehicle.
- No earlier damage to the vehicle is known.
- Nothing suggests the damage happened before the coverage started.
- The driver is named on the policy.
text:
Entry 1: Claim received for a collision at an intersection where the insured was turning left and was struck by an oncoming vehicle. The claimant reports a shoulder injury and is not represented by an attorney.

Entry 2: Reviewed the police report, which places the claimant in the vehicle at the time of the collision and records the other driver's account. The driver is named on the policy and the policy was in force on the date of loss.

Entry 3: Spoke with the claimant, who described the left turn, the oncoming car, and the impact to the driver's side front. The account matched what was given at the scene.

Entry 4: Two independent witnesses were contacted and both confirm the accident happened as the claimant described it. The other driver also gave a consistent version by phone.

Entry 5: Photos from the scene and the repair estimate show damage consistent with the reported impact. No prior damage to the vehicle is recorded in our files or in the inspection notes.

Entry 6: Nothing in the file suggests the damage predates the start of coverage. The vehicle inspection found no signs of earlier repairs in the affected areas.

Entry 7: Claimant reports pain in the right shoulder after the crash and was seen at an urgent care clinic the same day. The injury pattern appears consistent with the force and direction of the collision.

Entry 8: Treatment records show a usual course of physical therapy and follow-up visits. Reported pain has eased steadily as the claimant improved, and the provider notes a tapering of care.

Entry 9: Medical history reviewed. The claimant had a minor strain in the same shoulder several years ago that resolved fully with care and has not been treated since.

Entry 10: Claimant repeated the same account of the collision in each contact with our office. Based on the evidence reviewed, the injury and vehicle damage fit the reported loss, and the file is ready for the next settlement review.
